 Louisville City Holds Off Charleston Battery for Eastern Conference Crown
 By NICHOLAS MURRAY - nicholas.murray@uslsoccer.com , 11/14/26, 8:16PM EST 
 Share 
 Goalkeeper Ryan Schewe notches six-save shutout as goals by Ray Serrano, Manny Perez earn 2-0 victory at Patriots Point
 Louisville City FC captain Kyle Adams lifts the Eastern Conference trophy after his side's 2-0 victory against the Charleston Battery on Saturday night.
 CHARLESTON, S.C. – Ray Serrano and Manny Perez scored in either half as No. 4 seed Louisville City FC took a 2-0 victory against No. 2 seed the Charleston Battery on Saturday night in the Eastern Conference Final of the 2026 USL Championship Playoffs at Patriots Point as the visitors produced a stalwart defensive performance to earn a trip to the 2026 USL Championship Final. 
 The Battery came out on the front foot and carved out a pair of good early chances as Miguel Berry’s solo run ended in a low shot that was turned wide of the right post by LouCity goalkeeper Ryan Schewe. Jeremy Kelly also threatened for the hosts in the fifth minute, controlling cleverly in the left channel before curling a low shot to the far post that was also denied. 
 It was Louisville that took the lead in the ninth minute, however, as Taylor Davila lifted a pass in behind for Chris Donovan as he turned possession over in midfield, and after lifting the ball over the advancing goalkeeper, Donovan set up Serrano for a first-time finish. The Battery regained momentum soon after and almost leveled on the half-hour mark when Houssou Landry’s initial shot was saved before Colton Swan’s effort on the rebound was blocked behind for a corner. 
 The Battery’s pressure continued into the second half, although LouCity threatened to add a second just past the hour-mark when Babacar Niang made a surging run into the right side of the penalty area and forced a low save from Charleston’s Luis Zamudio. In the 67th minute, though, the visitors doubled their advantage when Perez delivered a pinpoint strike from the right side of the box that caromed in off the far post. 
 Charleston pressed to find a way back into the game, and with just under 10 minutes to go Laurent Kissiedou fired a first-time finish off a half-clearance that bounded into Schewe’s arms. Moments later, a goalmouth scramble following a corner kick saw efforts from Graham Smith, Berry and Joey Akpunonu be blocked before Kissiedou’s follow-up from the top of the box went wide. 
 Kissiedou then fired a long-range effort in stoppage time after Schewe had punched clear a cross from the center of his penalty area, only for the goalkeeper to get back and make the follow-up save, allowing the visitors to hold on and claim their fifth Eastern Conference title. 
 Takeaways 
 Charleston Battery – The hosts produced a strong performance in all ways but one as the finishing that had been the club’s hallmark at home throughout the season couldn’t find a way through the Louisville defense. The Battery were sharp early, and both Miguel Berry and Jeremy Kelly could have given their side the lead only to be denied by good saves inside the opening five minutes. As the game went on, though, chances fell by the wayside as the Battery held a 21-6 advantage in shots and more than 70% of possession but were unable to capitalize. 
 Louisville City FC – The visitors produced another outstanding defensive performance on the road that was reminiscent of their victory in the 2026 Prinx Tires USL Cup Final against Hartford Athletic. After Ray Serrano’s early goal got LouCity the lead after good work by Taylor Davila and Chris Donovan, the side was able to sit in and attempt to absorb pressure from the hosts. Louisville goalkeeper Ryan Schewe shone with six saves in the shutout, including a pair of crucial early stops before Serrano’s goal, but the side also recorded 50 clearances – led by 17-year-old Brandon Dayes with a team-high 10 – and blocked eight shots to earn a trip to the USL Championship Final and a chance at a record-setting third league crown. 
 Key Moment 
 Louisville City’s back line recorded three consecutive blocked shots by Brandon Daye, Tola Showunmi and Mukwelle Akale with six minutes to go to keep the Battery from pulling a goal back late and help Ryan Schewe preserve his shutout in the victory. 
 Key Stat 
 Louisville City’s 29.2% possession mark over the contest was its lowest in a game across the regular season and playoffs in the USL Championship this season as the side completed only 180 passes overall. 
 USL Championship Playoffs Player of the Game 
 Ryan Schewe, Louisville City FC – Schewe shone as he recorded a six-save shutout for the visitors while also recording two punched clearances and two high claims in the victory. 
 Scoring Summary
LOU – Ray Serrano (Chris Donovan) 9’
 LOU – Manny Perez (Zach Duncan) 68’
